title: AstraZeneca Strikes Up to $1.5 Billion AI Drug Discovery Deal With Insitro
key_facts: AstraZeneca is offering up to $1.5 billion to work with AI-focused insitro on new medicines for MASH and cardiomyopathies
They will search for drug targets using insitro's Virtual Human AI platform; AstraZeneca then advances candidates through development
insitro gets $40 million upfront and could earn $1.46 billion in milestones, plus royalties, per the company's announcement on 15 Oct 2026
Sharon Barr, executive VP and head of BioPharmaceuticals R&D at AstraZeneca, said selecting the target is one of the most critical R&D decisions
insitro already works with Bristol Myers Squibb and Eli Lilly; it laid off 22% of staff in May 2025 to extend its cash runway
quote_evidence: AstraZeneca is offering as much as $1.5 billion to work with AI-focused insitro to find new medicines for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and cardiomyopathies.
Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and could see $1.46 billion in milestones, plus royalties later on, according to the company's announcement on Thursday.
why_it_matters_hint: Most of the headline value depends on future milestones; the guaranteed part is $40 million.
notes: WSJ page blocked (401); read BioSpace. Reuters headline gives the $40 million upfront figure.
